answer: A field station log with research visit history works as the gate: visits logged at one field station for years. Each of 141 aliases needs its own visit histories, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The walnut check runs in the open: 141 fakes pay the full price 141 times, one honest agent pays once, and the thread trail in the ledger makes the fable cost visible to everyone.
